summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with nausea, diarrhea, and shortness of breath, found to have acute on chronic diastolic heart failure with pulmonary edema and a pansensitive Klebsiella urinary tract infection. She was treated with IV then oral diuresis; due to poor response to oral furosemide, she was transitioned to torsemide. The UTI was treated with antibiotics, and persistent dysuria was addressed with vaginal Estrace for suspected atrophic vaginitis. Her hypertension was managed with uptitrated hydralazine, and her bradycardia led to a reduction in metoprolol. She participated in physical therapy, improving her mobility to independently climb six stairs. Her chronic kidney disease and anemia were monitored, with nephrology follow-up planned for epogen consideration. She was discharged home with services, with plans for outpatient follow-up and medication adjustments.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage I through stage IV, or unspecified
Other specified noninflammatory disorders of vagina
